name: Jayesh Logistics Limited
sector: Industrial road and rail logistics, with Indo-Nepal corridor exposure
summary: Real revenue and fleet growth, but weak multi-year cash realization and senior debt constrain per-share value. BQS 4.7, GQS 5.0 after persistent-cash cap, IAS NS. G3 unresolved: favorable credit access plus temporary replacement deferral survives a stress that fails with immediate replacement capex. No actual default is asserted.
identity_note: ISIN, symbol, listing and 8,691,449 issued shares reconcile annual, shareholder filing, AGM and official security master. Standalone Indian GAAP; IPO cash already received. [S1,S2,S9,S11,S13]

quote.kind: Official final daily close, not live executable quote

score_note: Exact v3.0 arithmetic: BQS 4.74; GQS 5.80 capped at 5.0; IAS NS with 65% coverage and mathematical bound 2.635–5.785. No funding Fail cap because G3 is unresolved, and no midpoint for missing R.

gates.reason: Reviewed disclosures do not establish issuer diversion, fraud or abusive minority treatment. Historical filing/restatement corrections and separate promoter tax disclosures require entity-specific follow-through; allegations are not findings.

Core audited statements, source-specific restatements and cash classifications support bounded scoring. Two-sided historical classification differences are explained; uncertain tax access and replacement timing constrain forecasts rather than invalidating all historical figures.

150-day collection/13% margin stress has a 5.0284 crore gap even with favorable credit access at 4% replacement capex. After the large recent fleet addition, temporarily deferring replacement or limiting it to 1% for two years makes that same favorable-credit stress survive. Without credit recovery, deferral still leaves 2.0983 crore short. Actual credit access, drawing power and essential replacement schedule are unresolved; no forced Fail or Pass.

Observed official trades and eligible SM series refute an automatic suspension inference. Sparse participation, irregular trading, unknown missing dates and lot constraints limit execution at the illustrative 5 lakh size; current depth/spread is unavailable.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Jayesh is a growing, capital-intensive road/rail logistics operator with useful Indo-Nepal corridor experience, not a demonstrated cash-compounding franchise. Revenue reached ₹129.30 crore and the owned fleet expanded from 95 to 170 trucks, but three-year CFO/PAT is only 8.6% and the latest balance sheet carries ₹49.31 crore receivables and ₹45.13 crore debt. At the October 19 price of ₹125, a modest reported P/E does not resolve collection and debt-service risk. The ordinary linked base is unfunded; favorable credit-access or replacement-deferral alternatives survive but return less than the 15% hurdle. [S1,S2,S5,S12]

BQS is 4.7, GQS is 5.0 after the persistent-cash cap, and IAS is NS because there is no sufficiently supported funded base-case return. G3 is Hold — unresolved, not a claimed default: temporarily deferring replacement after the fleet expansion can make the same collection/margin stress survive when credit access is favorable. This is a speculative operational-improvement thesis, not an endorsed allocation or a credible financed 5×/10× case. Verified collections, accessible credits, bank drawing power and a fleet-specific essential replacement schedule would change the decision more than another order announcement.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Jayesh Logistics Limited, NSE SME symbol JAYESH, ISIN INE1AE401014. Cutoff: October 20, 2026, India reporting context; market reference is the October 19 close because October 20 is a market holiday. Price ₹125, issued capital 8,691,449 shares and market capitalization ₹108.64 crore. Analysis is standalone under Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not assumed Ind AS. No acquired subsidiary perimeter is invented. The five-year price horizon is October 19, 2026 to October 19, 2031; return hurdle 15% nominal annualized before investor taxes. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not a recommended holding. [S1,S2,S9,S12,S13]

G1 Conditional: no substantiated severe issuer integrity failure in the reviewed records, but historical filing corrections and separate promoter tax disclosures merit follow-through. G2 Conditional: audited core numbers support analysis, with explicit cash/restatement reconciliations and bounded forecast gaps. G3 Hold — unresolved: a funding gap depends materially on credit access and essential versus deferrable replacement capex. G4 Conditional: trading exists, but sparse participants and lot size constrain implementation.

Confidence is High on the latest signed statements, issued shares and loan transcription; Medium on long-history comparability, capital-return proxies, governance and historical liquidity; Low on the access/timing evidence needed to choose a funded future return case. Overall confidence for an investment conclusion is therefore Low. This does not turn every historical factor NS. Forecast uncertainty is separately high even where the input itself is verified.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5; MOAT 4; REV 7; DUR 6; CAP 4; CASH 3; BAL 3; EXEC 6; EARN 6; R NS; D 2; P 3; L 4. The accompanying factor audit gives evidence IDs, at least two material supporting facts and contrary evidence for each judgment. No missing factor is replaced with 5, no weights are redistributed, and none is scored 9–10 on a short or Medium-confidence history. [S1–S16]

BQS = 0.20×5 + 0.20×4 + 0.12×7 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×4 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×3 + 0.08×6 = 4.74, displayed 4.7, with 100% coverage and no BQS cap. GQS = 0.40×7 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×6 + 0.15×4 + 0.10×3 = 5.80; persistent CASH=3 caps the final at 5.0. The cap is based on multi-year conversion, not simply one expansion year or high capex.

IAS reuses unrounded BQS once: its known contributions are 0.25×4.74 + 0.20×2 + 0.10×3 + 0.10×4. R is NS, so coverage is 65%, raw/final IAS is NS and the mathematical missing-data bound is 2.635–5.785. This is not a forecast confidence interval or a point ranking. G3 is unresolved, so no funding-failure cap is asserted; even a cap would not replace a missing score.

A one-point change in CAP and BAL together moves BQS by 0.20 and IAS's quality contribution by 0.05. CAP ±1 changes raw GQS by 0.15, still capped at 5.0. Nearby historical ranks should therefore not be treated as precise economic separations. Only BQS/GQS are provisionally comparable; IAS and an investment-matrix cell remain withheld.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Jayesh earns fees for freight transport using owned and hired vehicles, rail forwarding and ancillary non-freight logistics such as customs/handling and coordination. Its footprint is especially relevant to industrial movements and the Indo-Nepal corridor. Steel, infrastructure and cement account for most of the FY2025 industry mix; this is not a diversified consumer-parcel franchise. The issuer reports 200+ customers, but the top ten supplied 76.45% of FY2025 revenue, versus 69.84% in FY2024. A customer count does not remove concentration. [S1,S2]

FY2026 freight revenue was ₹98.4748 crore, up from ₹78.2757 crore; non-freight fell to ₹30.8208 crore from ₹33.6064 crore. Freight growth therefore drove the total increase. The owned fleet expanded from 95 to 170 trucks, supplemented by hired capacity. Operating costs include outside freight, trip expenses, fuel-related running costs, drivers, tyres, vehicle repairs, container and railway charges. Gross revenue is economically larger than the retained value added, so margins and capital needed to collect the bill matter alongside turnover. [S1]

Money is made by securing industrial/customer movements, planning routes and loading, using capacity efficiently and controlling operating costs. Money is collected later: closing receivables equaled about 139 days of annual sales in March 2026. SAIL's disclosed 30-day terms apply to that contract, not automatically to the entire book. FY2025 Indo-Nepal revenue share of 63.53% is historical; the very high June 2025 quarter share is seasonal and is not substituted for a verified FY2026 mix. No independently measured market-share denominator was established.

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is corridor know-how and execution reliability: established industrial relationships, customs/transport coordination, a mix of owned and hired vehicles and integrated dispatch/IT can reduce friction for customers. Mechanism → evidence: the business has delivered multi-year revenue expansion and secured named industrial contracts. Durability → failure mode: competitors can hire trucks, build relationships and adopt logistics software; large customers can retender, shift volumes or demand price reductions. A 170-truck fleet is useful capacity, not a self-proving network moat. SMARTSYS and fuel-escalation protection are management claims unless demonstrated by sustained utilization and net economics. [S1,S2,S7,S8]

The prospectus lists Ritco Logistics and SJ Logistics as broad listed comparators, while acknowledging differences in mix and size. VRL's official parcel/LTL/FTL offering illustrates the network breadth available elsewhere; its reported scale is not a matched financial comparison or a reason to transplant its multiple. Jayesh is more concentrated in industrial/cross-border movements, and neither reported customer logos nor a low IPO peer P/E establishes relative quality. October 2025 peer valuation statistics are stale for the present cutoff. [S2,S16]

Contrary evidence to an entirely undifferentiated view is real scaling and repeat customer access. Contrary evidence to a strong-moat view is rising top-ten dependence, weaker cash realization and no clean price/volume or customer-retention cohort evidence. MOAT=4 therefore reflects useful but contestable capability, not an allegation that the company adds no value. A stronger score would require repeatable excess returns after full fleet and working-capital costs, diversified recurring business and evidence that competitors cannot easily replicate the service economics.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Operating revenue, ₹ crore: FY2021 56.4432; FY2022 51.2684; FY2023 60.3413; FY2024 88.2591; FY2025 111.8821; FY2026 129.2956. The chosen five-year window uses six observations: 56.4432→129.2956 gives 18.03% CAGR. The three-year comparison, 60.3413→129.2956, gives 28.92%; it is disclosed but not substituted to obtain a higher factor. Ten-year CAGR is ND. Annual additions are FY2022 ₹-5.1748, FY2023 ₹+9.0729, FY2024 ₹+27.9178, FY2025 ₹+23.6230, FY2026 ₹+17.4135, all crore. FY2026 growth is 15.56%. [S1–S4]

FY2021 includes pandemic conditions, but its revenue was above FY2020's ₹53.7445 crore. No arbitrary pandemic correction or small-base penalty is imposed. Original and restated accounting bases remain labeled. No material acquired revenue is included in the reviewed history; however, the available reporting does not fully separate tonnage, routes, tariffs, pass-through fuel and mix, so the series is reported same-issuer growth rather than an invented constant-price organic-volume metric.

The latest comparable halves are uneven: H1 FY2026 ₹59.33 crore against derived H1 FY2025 ₹44.8162 crore, approximately +32.39%; H2 FY2026 ₹69.9656 crore against ₹67.0659 crore, +4.32%. Prior-half comparatives are management-prepared/unaudited; the March 2026 half is a balancing figure. This does not support a sustained trajectory bonus or penalty. A full FY2027 interim was not verified by the cutoff, so no seasonal half is annualized into a current TTM. [S5,S10]

Freight grew 25.80% while non-freight declined 8.29%. FY2025 order count fell from 909 to 832 while average billing rose, but the prospectus explains changing monthly non-freight versus per-trip freight invoicing. That is not a homogeneous volume/pricing-power bridge. REV remains 7 under the exact 15–20% starting band, with zero trajectory adjustment.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The near-term opportunity is to use the expanded fleet more productively and convert actual industrial traffic into cash, not simply to buy another block of trucks. The model's ordinary revenue path grows 8%, 10%, 10%, 8%, 6% and 6% across FY2027 through the FY2032 run-rate used at the October 2031 exit; terminal annualized revenue is ₹205.04 crore. Fleet productivity is not independently disclosed, so ₹170 crore of initial revenue capacity is an analyst headroom assumption, not the coincidental 170-truck count presented as certified capacity. Beyond this allowance, incremental revenue requires additional capital at 0.25 times the revenue increment, plus replacement capex and working capital. [S1,S2]

The operating driver path requires industrial contracts, vehicle utilization, route density, hired-fleet availability and collections to improve together. SAIL and Dalmia provide access, but their variable quantities and customer rights make face values unsuitable as guaranteed revenue. The bull path to ₹293.31 crore additionally needs collection days to fall toward 100, advances to decline to 7% of sales and EBITDA margin to reach 16%; it is not management guidance or the default outcome. [S7,S8]

Capital returns are a constraint. The transparent financial-capital proxy gives about 11.51% incremental NOPAT return over three years and 11.80% over five, versus an explicitly assumed 12–16% capital-cost range. Late purchases depress the current comparison, but the next fleet cohort must prove better utilization and cash return, not just accounting margin. Approximately 18% historical revenue growth with an 11.5% incremental-return proxy would require about 157% reinvestment under a stable-economics growth≈reinvestment×return check, indicating dependence on external finance rather than a precise forecast identity.

GQS raw 5.80 is capped at 5.0 because persistent cash realization is weak. Growth is real, but the evidence does not yet show self-funding intrinsic-value-per-share compounding. Replacing genuine capex with free revenue, or adding IPO proceeds a second time, would falsely improve this assessment.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The latest statutory audit is unmodified and the reviewed CARO report does not report fraud or borrowing default. It notes some delays in statutory payments, but none remaining undisputed for more than six months. GGPS was appointed in September 2024 for the stated five-year tenure; May 2026 internal/secretarial appointments are not misdescribed as a statutory auditor resignation. These are positive controls, not proof that governance risk is absent. [S1,S17]

March 2026 promoter-group ownership was 71.22% and the primary pattern disclosed no pledge, warrants, convertibles or ESOPs, although lock-ins existed. A later primary September pattern was not verified, so this is not a current pledge guarantee. Directors' remuneration rose to ₹1.02 crore from ₹0.83 crore; the disclosed related furniture purchase, services, salary, CSR and loans are assessed as related-party exposure, not automatically abuse. The ₹1.3083 crore director-loan balance is already inside debt, and outstanding related remuneration sits inside employee liabilities. [S1,S11]

Promises versus delivery: the October 2025 IPO allocated ₹8.8475 crore to trailers, fully used by March 2026; ₹11.2375 crore WC and ₹3.8834 crore general corporate purposes were also fully used. SMARTSYS phase II had used ₹0.1331 of ₹0.7150 crore, leaving ₹0.5819 crore; deployment remains incomplete at that dated certificate. Fleet count reached 170 versus 95, but current receivables and weak CFO mean physical execution has not yet translated into equivalent cash delivery. July/September 2026 Dalmia/SAIL orders are awarded opportunities, not proof of recognized or collected revenue. [S1,S6–S8]

The prospectus separately discloses prior statutory-filing errors and corrective measures, as well as tax proceedings involving promoters/directors. These are not issuer tax debt, and tax allegations are not established issuer misconduct. The prospectus records a response to the tax authority, but no subsequent final outcome was verified and its summary/detail amounts do not fully reconcile. G1 remains Conditional rather than failed; the latest nil issuer contingencies do not prove resolution of a promoter's personal/corporate matter.

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical bridge, ₹ crore, standalone:
FY2021: revenue 56.4432; core EBITDA 5.9396; core EBIT 2.7413; reported PAT 0.8426; normalized PAT 1.0637; comparable CFO 1.2129; reported capex 0.0537.
FY2022: revenue 51.2684; core EBITDA 4.6500; core EBIT 1.8739; reported PAT 0.9673; normalized PAT 0.6541; comparable CFO 0.9411; reported capex 0.0767.
FY2023: revenue 60.3413; core EBITDA 4.7769; core EBIT 2.9039; reported PAT 1.0906; normalized PAT 1.0903; comparable CFO 4.8326; reported capex 2.3734.
FY2024: revenue 88.2591; core EBITDA 10.4040; core EBIT 6.4254; reported PAT 3.1633; normalized PAT 3.2561; comparable CFO 2.6640; reported capex 15.6037.
FY2025: revenue 111.8821; core EBITDA 16.9297; core EBIT 12.3697; reported PAT 7.2213; normalized PAT 7.1370; comparable CFO 3.9003; reported capex 1.1621.
FY2026: revenue 129.2956; core EBITDA 19.9669; core EBIT 15.2170; reported PAT 10.0845; normalized PAT 9.2177; comparable CFO -4.7992; reported capex 36.4099.
Definitions: core EBIT = PBT + finance cost − other income; core EBITDA adds D&A; normalized PAT removes all other income and applies the analytical 25.17% tax rate. This is not a claim that each original year's statutory rate was wrong. Service contribution before employee/other costs is ₹24.1752 crore in FY2026, but it is not relabeled a standardized gross-profit metric without a consistent historical definition. [S1–S4]

FY2026 revenue rose 15.56%, core EBITDA 17.94% and core EBIT 23.02%, while reported PAT rose 39.65%. Lower effective tax and ₹0.1936 crore insurance gain contribute to the faster PAT growth. Reported weighted EPS ₹13.83 uses 7,289,679 shares; PAT/current 8,691,449 shares is ₹11.6039. The prior actual closing shares were 6,344,449, so FY2025 PAT/then-closing shares was about ₹11.38: much less impressive per-share progress than the profit growth alone. The 10:1 bonus is already reflected in the restated history; old unadjusted EPS must not be compared. [S1,S2]

CFO reconciliation: pre-WC ₹19.9968 crore minus net operating-stock absorption ₹20.9371 crore gives cash before tax −₹0.9403 crore; taxes ₹3.8589 crore leave CFO −₹4.7992 crore. Receivables absorbed ₹11.5659 crore, advances ₹10.3421 crore and reduced payables ₹1.8847 crore; other liability growth and FD/current-asset releases partially offset them. Reported CFO plus CFI −₹33.4347 crore plus CFF ₹38.9877 crore reconciles cash ₹1.2035→₹1.9572 crore. Capex cannot explain negative CFO. [S1]

Cash classifications matter. FY2022 reported CFO ₹3.0620709 crore includes borrowing ₹2.1210016 crore; removing it once gives comparable ₹0.9410693 crore. FY2021's reclassified comparative matches the original to about ₹94. FY2025 annual versus restated CFO differs by ₹0.1022 crore with an equal opposite investing reclassification, not missing cash. FY2026 CFO includes a ₹2.2767 crore capital-creditor increase and ₹1 crore prior capital-advance release, while reported capex matches gross additions. An illustrative transfer of both capital items out of CFO and capex yields CFO −₹8.0759 crore and cash-capex proxy ₹33.1332 crore, leaving the same −₹41.2091 crore CFO-less-capex total. Bank-paid timing and other non-operating classifications are not independently verified, so this is a classification diagnostic, not a new accounting accusation.

Receivables over six months improved to ₹5.2636 crore from ₹8.4609 crore, including ₹2.80 crore over two years. This contrary improvement is retained even though closing days rose from about 123.2 to 139.2. The financial-capital proxy rose from ₹16.8307 crore in FY2023 to ₹96.8509 crore in FY2026; incremental NOPAT returns are 11.51% over three years and 11.80% over five. Average-capital FY2026 return is 16.16%. It retains restricted/tax capital, and late fleet deployment limits immediate interpretation.

Every opening claim is included once: ordinary trade/statutory/employee/customer balances remain in operating WC; 18 loans, current maturities, CC and director loans are financing; tax ₹0.0629 crore, net gratuity ₹0.0299 crore and capital creditor ₹2.2767 crore have explicit payment dates. Income-tax asset ₹0.1942 crore and government asset ₹3.4338 crore are excluded centrally and recovered/offset once only in favorable sensitivities. Legacy DTL ₹0.8042 crore is retained at exit. Lien FD, other FD, security deposits and earmarked IPO funds are not freely spendable. The leasehold office is carried at its disclosed long-lease acquisition cost; no undisclosed IFRS-style lease liability is invented.

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The October 19 price is ₹125, market cap ₹108.64 crore. Using explicitly dated March debt and ordinary cash gives EV ₹153.33 crore, reported P/E 10.77x, normalized P/E 11.79x, EV/core EBITDA 7.68x, EV/core EBIT 10.08x and P/B 2.08x. These are not current October net-debt observations. Normalized tax is 25.17%; ₹0.3133 crore other income is excluded from the historical core cross-check. Negative latest CFO-less-capex makes a positive FCF-yield argument inappropriate. [S1,S12,S13]

The model starts with actual March claims and rolls each month through October 19, 2031. It includes the 18-loan repayment schedule, interest on same-month CC draws, current debt maturities, existing line capacity only, new and old tax, WC, replacement/growth capex, ERP earmarks, capital creditors, security deposit and the approved dividend. The September record date precedes entry, so the new investor receives no dividend credit. Amounts forecast for April–October are not represented as observed receipts or missed payments.

Ordinary base: growth 8/10/10/8/6/6%, 15% EBITDA margin, receivable days 125 then 120, existing advance/payable ratios, replacement capex 4% of sales and additional growth capex above the assumed initial headroom. The terminal multiple is 8x EBIT. It develops a ₹1.3303 crore peak cash gap, so shareholder IRR and entry price are NS. Its arithmetic terminal output is not an achievable funded fair value.

Bear: initial revenue −10%, 12% margin and receivables 160 days gradually improving to 140, with 6x EBIT. The ₹9.5496 crore gap prevents an investor IRR. Bull: growth 18/18/16/14/12/10%, 16% margin, collection days 115→100, advances 7% of sales and 10x EBIT; it funds itself in this model and gives 26.64% annualized return. That is a jointly favorable collection/utilization case, not the supported base.

Funded alternatives make the uncertainty visible. Full early recovery of government credits and one-time matched tax use, with the ordinary operating base, gives 11.29% return and ₹213.40 exit price. The terminal bridge is EV ₹182.7165 + cash ₹3.5662 − debt 0 − legacy DTL 0.8042 = equity ₹185.4785 crore, divided by 0.8691449 crore shares. Its 12/15/18% hurdle entry prices are ₹121.10/₹106.11/₹93.29. Deferring replacement for two years without recovering those credits yields 13.05% and a 15% hurdle price ₹114.76. These conditional ₹106–115 diagnostics are not buy levels that resolve G3.

Hypothetical ₹5 crore net rescue equity, grossed up for 3% fees at ₹125 or ₹100, funds the ordinary case but dilutes shares to 0.9103820 or 0.9206913 crore and returns about 10.50% or 10.25%. This is an explicitly counterfactual financing intervention, not an announced/received issue. No option/warrant cash is invented. Two-way growth/multiple sensitivities rerun funding; the ordinary 0–40% growth reverse grid finds no funded 15% crossing at 6/8/10x. A separate favorable-credit matrix shows what changes when funding access is relaxed.

Book equity is ₹52.16 crore or about ₹60.02 per current share, not a liquidation floor. As a severe recovery cross-check, 65% of net PPE, 80% of receivables, 50% of advances and all reported cash/other FD, zero intangible/CWIP recovery, less all booked liabilities yields only about ₹20.89 per share before sale costs, taxes and timing. Those haircuts are assumptions, not appraisals; collateral cash can repay creditors in this liquidation bridge but is never simultaneously free operating cash. Normalized earnings multiples and asset support therefore do not overturn the funding-sensitive return conclusion.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The central loss mechanism is industrial/customer or border disruption → weaker vehicle utilization and slower receipts → insufficient cash for secured amortization and necessary operating costs → forced asset sales or dilutive finance. Concentrated customers, 139-day closing receivables and weak cumulative cash conversion make that mechanism credible, without alleging today's default. The most important thesis-break variable is cash collected after financing the operating cycle, not headline orders. [S1,S2]

The restrained test keeps revenue flat, carries no receivable write-off, renews the existing CC line and stops growth capex. It moves EBITDA margin from 15.44% to 13% and receivables from 139.2 to 150 days. With 4% replacement capex the gap is ₹10.0557 crore. Allowing full early government-asset recovery, one-time income-tax credits, director-loan rollover and March capital-creditor settlement still leaves ₹5.0284 crore short. Lower interest or 3% replacement alone does not eliminate the gap. This is a scenario from March balances, not an assertion that any forecast negative month actually occurred.

The strongest disconfirmation of a forced insolvency view is replacement flexibility. Vehicle purchases were ₹30.0004 crore in FY2026, and recurring repairs, tyres and HCV AMC already remain in operating expense. A new fleet need not spend 4% of sales on immediate annual replacement. With the same 150-day/13% stress and favorable credit access, zero replacement for two years followed by 4%, or 1% for two years followed by 4%, survives. The latter still produces about -5.66% annualized investor loss and a ₹93.40 terminal price, approximately 25.3% below entry. Without government/tax-credit recovery, the zero-then-normal replacement case still has a ₹2.0983 crore gap. Therefore actual credit access and the essential replacement schedule can change survival: G3 remains unresolved, not mechanically Pass or Fail.

A separate severe boundary cuts revenue 20%, margin to 10%, pushes collections to 180 days, applies a 10% opening receivable impairment and removes CC renewal. Its ₹36.32 crore gap is a tail boundary, not the sole gate basis. Opening impairment is deducted from recoverable stock and PAT once; only subsequent replacement WC consumes cash. Poor asset recovery can permanently impair equity even when an operating countercase survives. Overall impairment risk is High, with meaningful recovery uncertainty rather than an invented probability or guaranteed zero value.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× or 10× share-price outcome over five years requires approximately 38.0% or 58.5% annualized price growth, distinct from revenue growth. With today's issued shares unchanged, ₹108.64 crore market cap would need to become ₹543.22 crore or ₹1086.43 crore. At 8x terminal EBIT and the favorable-credit case's cash/debt bridge and forward EBIT margin, the arithmetic requires roughly ₹606 crore or ₹1216 crore annual revenue. [S1,S12,S13]

Using FY2026 sales as a transparent five-year scaling illustration implies about 36.2% or 56.6% annual revenue growth. That illustration is not the exact calendar-based investor model and does not establish funding. It requires additional fleet/contractor capacity, route/customer access, cash advances, maintenance and receivables while servicing secured lenders. Current core cash realization is inconsistent with assuming all that growth funds itself.

The bullish operating case can exceed the 15% hurdle but does not reach 5×, and it already assumes better collections, utilization and margin together. Higher multiples merely transfer the burden to sustained superior business economics; rescue equity increases the share denominator. No independently verified market-share/capacity path or financed 5×/10× scenario is demonstrated. Classification: speculative / unsupported, rather than a claim that such an outcome is impossible.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The structured monitoring register records eight specific baselines, expected evidence, warning conditions and thesis breaks. These are research checkpoints, not trade instructions or a monitoring automation. Review the next comparable half-year rather than extrapolating a seasonal quarter, and distinguish revenue booked from tonnage billed and cash received. The reference collection improvement is 120–125 days; 150 days combined with a 13% margin is a model warning to investigate, not proof of default. [S1,S5]

The immediate funding evidence is more useful than another headline order: obtain the dated loan/CC drawing-power position, actual capital-creditor settlement, tax/government-credit nature and receipts, and a vehicle-age/utilization schedule showing which replacement spending is genuinely essential. Retain the favorable deferral countercase unless contrary operating evidence rules it out. Improving aged balances is real contrary evidence and should not be discarded simply because aggregate receivables rose.

Check ERP deployment against its permitted IPO use, and reconcile SAIL/Dalmia invoicing with quantity variability and collections. Update promoter encumbrances from a primary pattern rather than assuming March status remains current; assess any legal change at the correct entity. Finally, refresh 20/60-session traded values, lot size, restrictions and actual depth for the user's real position. A price decrease alone does not prove funds are accessible; an alert is a request to revisit evidence, not an automatic buy/sell action.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: mixed-quality, funding-sensitive logistics operator; speculative improvement research, not a demonstrated compounder and not a point-ranked investment. BQS 4.7 and capped GQS 5.0 describe the historical business and growth evidence. IAS is NS because R cannot be assigned from an unfunded ordinary base or an unverified favorable alternative. Under the framework, missing IAS and unresolved G3 precede the classification matrix; a numerical weak-setup cell is not fabricated.

The business has scaled, core operating earnings are genuine in the reviewed accounts, older receivable ageing improved and the new fleet provides replacement flexibility. Those positives prevent an automatic integrity or funding Fail. They do not erase recurring weak cash conversion, concentration, senior debt obligations or the possibility of dilutive financing. BAL=3 records evidenced fragility, while the precise survival verdict remains unresolved because key assumptions can change it. [S1,S2]

Conditional action is to resolve collectability, legally accessible credits, actual bank drawing power and minimum replacement needs before treating the reported P/E as investable. The financed favorable cases at the reference price return about 11.3% or 13.0%, below the 15% hurdle; the bull is much stronger but needs simultaneous operational improvement. Lower conditional entry diagnostics are not recommendations and do not cure missing funding evidence. Refresh both the capital bridge and liquidity for the user's actual position before any implementation decision. No trade, target allocation or promised monitoring follows from this report.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The evidence hierarchy is current signed annual/results and IPO-use records, final prospectus/restated accounts and original FY2021–22 scans, then dated contract/shareholding filings and official NSE trading/status data. The source ledger gives source-specific dates, scope, locators, confidence and limitations. Historical originals FY2023–25 were located, but the analysis uses the prospectus restatements and latest annual comparatives instead of claiming every scan was read. Only the official VRL overview is added for the specific peer-context gap; no stale peer multiple is treated as current. [S1–S18]

Material unresolved items are current cash and drawing power after March, legal/timing access to government and income-tax assets, the essential replacement schedule for the expanded fleet, actual capital-creditor/dividend settlement timing, later primary promoter pledges, and subsequent promoter-specific tax outcomes. The old tax table/detail amount inconsistency is not silently reconciled to a preferred number. There is no verified FY2027 interim, ten-year comparable series, homogeneous price/volume split, current audited peer-multiple set or executable consolidated backlog roll-forward.

Analyst assumptions include 25.17% future tax, selected variable/CC/director rates, 5.5% collateral-deposit yield, monthly settlement timing, 12–16% capital-cost reference, 14% depreciation on the modeled net asset base with 12/16% sensitivity, 6–10x terminal EBIT, collection/advance ratios and capex productivity. Replacement capex is distinct from expensed repairs. Full credit recovery and hypothetical equity are sensitivities, not verified money; canceled ERP spending does not free earmarks. Model shortfalls are conditional research outputs, not actual default findings.

All annual/monthly cash, debt, WC, earmark, claim, dilution and terminal bridges are checked. Terminal recovery values exclude collateral/credit balances not realized in a scenario. Investor taxes and precise market impact are not estimated; separate execution-cost sensitivity shows the effect of 1–2% entry and exit friction on financed returns. Final IAS remains incomplete rather than hiding these material choices inside a single fair-value estimate.

GOV.reason: Unmodified accounts, disclosed proceeds use and no issuer proceeding/default finding support adequate conduct. Earlier statutory/restatement corrections, concentrated control and promoter-specific unresolved tax disclosures limit a stronger stewardship assessment. RPTs alone are not misconduct.

MOAT.reason: Cross-border execution experience and an owned/hired fleet provide useful service capability. Concentrated customers, contestable freight pricing, declining heterogeneous order counts and much larger transport networks leave durable excess pricing or switching power unproven; real revenue growth is the contrary positive.

REV.reason: Preselected FY2021–26 reported operating CAGR is 18.03%, starting score 7. FY2021 revenue was above FY2020, not an obvious trough. H1 grew 32.4% but H2 only 4.3%, so no sustained plus/minus trajectory adjustment is justified. Three-year 28.92% is shown, not cherry-picked.

DUR.reason: Expanded fleet, industrial demand and SAIL/Dalmia access provide real avenues to deploy capacity. Customer and Nepal corridor concentration, variable-volume contracts and working-capital-intensive access constrain the runway. Announced order totals are not a funded backlog.

CAP.reason: Three-/five-year incremental capital returns around 11.5%/11.8% are slightly below the explicit 12–16% capital-cost range; capital tied in receivables and the new fleet is substantial. FY2026 average capital return is about 16.2%, and late additions may improve future economics, so persistent destruction is not established.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO/PAT of 8.6% and five-year comparable 33.5%, with FY2026 negative CFO and rising closing collection days, establish persistent weak realization. Positive earlier cash and improving older ageing are contrary evidence, but not enough to remove the cash-quality cap. Capex is separate from CFO.

BAL.reason: Only 0.4402 crore ordinary opening cash faces 10.8719 crore current term maturities and a thin existing line. Ordinary base/stress funding gaps establish fragility, not missingness. Favorable credit access plus temporary replacement deferral survives, so BAL is weak but G3 is unresolved rather than mechanically failed.

EXEC.reason: Fleet grew from 95 to 170 and trailer/WC IPO objects were used; delivered revenue and new industrial orders demonstrate commercial execution. ERP remains partly unspent, recent half-year growth slowed and collection delivery lags accounting profit. Longer-term utilization and per-share returns remain to be proven.

EARN.reason: Core operating earnings expanded with freight revenue and margins; other income is small. FY2026 profit growth also benefits from a lower effective tax rate, full-year new-fleet costs are not yet in history, and IPO dilution makes weighted EPS look stronger than current-share EPS. Cash weakness is separately scored in CASH.

R.reason: The ordinary linked base is unfunded, so assigning it an investor IRR would be false. Credit-access and replacement-deferral variants are useful funded diagnostics, but neither has enough dated access/replacement evidence to become the supported return case. R and IAS remain NS, not a numerical funding cap masquerading as a return.

D.reason: Credible collection/margin stress can require financing and financed adverse countercases still lose value. Owned assets and the ability to defer replacement are recovery positives, but secured lenders, concentrated collection risk and uncertain shareholder financing make downside resilience poor. No actual default is asserted.

P.reason: A roughly 10.8x reported P/E is not an extreme headline price, but several operating/collection/capital-access conditions must improve together to support the hurdle. Favorable credit access yields only 11.3% and replacement-deferral base about 13.0%; the bull can outperform, showing demanding rather than impossible expectations.

L.reason: The conservative 60-session theoretical 9.08-day exit starts at 5. One explicit point downgrade reflects sparse participation, irregular-trading alerts and a 1,000-share lot worth more than a 5% daily slice. Last-20-session capacity is weaker at 11.49 days; no live executable-depth claim is made.

Q.reason: Final unrounded BQS reused exactly once in IAS.

confidence.forecast_uncertainty: High uncertainty, separate from confidence in reported historical inputs

notes: No investor IRR or entry price is assigned to an unfunded path. Terminal prices for such paths are unfinanced operating diagnostics, not realizable shareholder values. Hypothetical equity cases are separate from verified funding.
The existing cash-credit limit of 11.8 crore assumes eligible drawing power and renewal. Sanctioned headroom is not independently bank-verified available money; a no-headroom alternative is shown.

All April 2026–October 2031 cash balances are scenarios from audited March 2026 stocks, not observed current cash. The dividend record date predates the entry date, so the new investor receives no credit.

The first 12 months honor disclosed current term principal of 10.8719 crore. One floating-loan EMI is close to principal-only amortization; principal plus interest is used centrally and the nominal EMI with maturity balloon is tested separately.

Full government-credit recovery is an optimistic countercase, not evidence of legal tax matching. Restricted and earmarked cash is never freely spent. The opening deferred-tax liability is retained once as a terminal claim.

Margins, growth, collection days, replacement capex and 14% depreciation on net book value are analyst assumptions. Repairs and tyres remain in operating expense and are not counted as replacement capex. Temporary replacement deferral is tested because 75 trucks were added during FY2026. Debt service and opening claims come from audited disclosures. Model shortfalls are not findings of actual default.
